title: CDS-Skill SignalPacket
description: The perception packet. This is the ONLY input the deterministic engine accepts. It is produced by the host LLM (or by a human annotator) using references/prompts/detect.md and the anchored rubric in references/codebook.md. Every 0-1 field must follow the codebook anchors; the engine never invents a perceptual judgement of its own. Separating perception (LLM, fallible, measured) from arithmetic (engine, deterministic, tested) is what makes the index reproducible and the perception auditable.

run_id.description: Session-scoped identifier shared by every record of one run.

detected_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp. Optional; the engine stamps one when absent.

annotator.description: Who produced this packet: a model id, 'human:<id>', or 'gold'. Recorded verbatim in the log so model-generated and human-generated packets are never confused.

type.description: 'none' means no CDS-relevant conflict was perceived. internal_contradiction is deliberately NOT a member: a self-inconsistent answer is a consistency defect, not a stance-evidence conflict, and it is routed through consistency_gate instead.

opposition.description: How directly the new element contradicts the stance, on the codebook anchor scale. 0 = merely different topic; 1 = logically incompatible with the same claim under the same conditions.

specificity.description: How concrete and falsifiable the contradiction is. 0 = vague unease; 1 = names a quantity, source, date or mechanism that can be checked.

rationale.description: One sentence naming the two elements that clash. Required by the codebook discipline even though the schema cannot enforce it.

stance.description: The position the new element conflicts with. It is EXTRACTED from the context, never asserted by the perceiver: `anchor` names the span it was read off, and a packet that names a position without pointing at one is capped by the anchor_required gate and will not interrupt a user. Absent when relation.type is 'none' or 'evidence_vs_evidence'.

source.description: Where the stance came from: prior_conversation | user_message | memory | tool_output | system_prompt | normative_prior. The last is the single exemption from the extraction rule: a mainstream value norm the agent holds as a baseline, which by definition cannot be read out of a conversation that does not mention it. It travels on its own channel and is never reported as dissonance.

anchor.description: The verbatim span in the context that the claim is read off: an earlier message of the agent's own, the user's words, a memory entry, a tool output, or the system prompt. Required for evidence_vs_stance, user_hint_vs_stance and memory_vs_current. This field is what separates an observation from an invention - without it the engine would be reasoning about a position nobody ever held.

normative_basis.description: With source=normative_prior, a short clause naming the mainstream norm the judgement rests on, e.g. 不得对平民实施暴力. Reported on the card so the reader can see which norm is being invoked rather than being told one exists.

commitment.description: How tightly the agent is bound to the claim. 0 = a passing suggestion; 1 = a load-bearing premise of its plan.

public_commitment.description: How visibly the agent has already asserted the claim to this user. Separate from commitment because public assertion raises the social cost of revision.

volition.description: Free-choice signal. 1 = the agent itself chose this position among alternatives it considered. 0 = the position was assigned by the user, the system prompt, or a tool.

self_relevance.description: How far the claim is the agent's own product rather than a fact it merely relayed.

evidence.description: Elements bearing on the stance. Required and non-empty for every conflict type except 'none'. The evaluator scores all of these, and reports the per-dimension detail, so a single bad credibility guess is visible rather than hidden inside an average.

carries_conflict.description: False for consonant evidence included for context. Only carrying evidence feeds the evaluator.

novelty.description: How much of this is information the agent did not already hold. Repeated restatement of a known objection scores low; the v0.1 design rewarded repetition, which opened a sycophancy channel and has been removed.

quote.description: Verbatim span from the context that the rating is anchored on.

user_pressure.description: Social pressure to agree with the user. Deliberately NOT a term of the tension index: arousal should not depend on being nagged, but pressure does bias which reduction strategy is chosen. The engine therefore logs it as a moderator and routes on it.

evidence_conflict_unresolved.description: How far the evidence items contradict each other rather than the stance, leaving no determinate direction. High values force suspend_and_verify.

internal_contradiction.description: Self-inconsistency inside the agent's own current output. Reported on its own channel and never added to the tension index.

confidence.description: The annotator's confidence in its own packet. Logged for error analysis; never enters the arithmetic.

ambiguities.description: What the annotator could not determine from the available context.
